title: Task-report application support comes only from Hunch's own rule evaluation, never from agent claims or passing commands
context: The release plan for task contribution reports requires a 'supported application' grade with independent evidence linking a delivered lesson to the action, checked against a declared validation rule; file overlap alone is insufficient. Codex's implementation left this pending: claims were agent-reported and checks were command results with no link to the lesson.
decision: runReportConformance (src/core/taskReportEvidence.ts) evaluates each delivered constraint/decision revision's OWN declared rule against the working tree's changes vs HEAD: a constraint's forbids matcher over the added lines of its scoped changed files; a decision's conformance predicates over the current working graph, only when a predicate subject is defined in a changed file. Outcomes: satisfied | violated | not-exercised | unavailable, bound to a bounded source snapshot and stored as a 'conformance' report event. A claim becomes rule-supported only while a satisfied evaluation of the same record revision matches the current source; the attribution stays agent-reported. Violations are always shown on the card. Scope-only constraints and changed stored revisions are 'unavailable', never evaluated in place. It runs automatically on a completed finish (CLI, MCP hunch_task, engine API) and via `hunch task conform`; no MCP tool accepts a submitted verdict.
consequences: Support exists only for lessons with a machine-checkable rule; most prose-only decisions stay agent-reported
Finish now performs a git diff and, for decisions with predicates, a working-tree repo scan; failures are disclosed as unknowns and never block finish
alternatives_rejected: Agent-declared `validated_by: check_id` linking a claim to a passing command: the linkage is still the agent's choice, so a passing unrelated command could upgrade an application
Upgrading attribution when a claim's record scope overlaps changed files: file overlap alone is explicitly insufficient in the plan's evidence rules
Treating any passing local check as support for all claims in the task: the HTML/card must not upgrade agent wording on the strength of an unrelated pass
